items.followUp: What is meant by the least count of a measuring instrument?

rubric.why: Recognises that significant figures include the certain digits.
rubric.description: States that the certain digits are included.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the certain digits.

rubric.why: Identifies the final doubtful digit in the measurement.
rubric.description: States that the first uncertain (doubtful) digit is included.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the uncertain digit.

modelAnswer: Significant figures in a measurement are all the certain digits plus the first uncertain (doubtful) digit.

items.followUp: Differentiate between uniform and non-uniform acceleration.

rubric.why: Positive acceleration means velocity increases with time.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that velocity or speed increases with time.

rubric.why: Negative acceleration means velocity decreases with time.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that velocity or speed decreases with time.

modelAnswer: Positive acceleration occurs when the velocity of a body increases with time.
Negative acceleration occurs when the velocity of a body decreases with time.

items.followUp: Define speed and write its SI unit.

rubric.why: Velocity is defined as displacement changing per unit time.
rubric.description: Defines velocity as the rate of change of displacement with time.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct definition.

rubric.why: The SI unit of velocity is metre per second.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct unit.

modelAnswer: Velocity is the rate of change of displacement with time in a particular direction.
Its SI unit is metre per second (m/s).

items.followUp: State Newton’s second law of motion and write the SI unit of force.

rubric.why: Force is described as a push or pull that changes or tends to change a body's state.
rubric.description: Defines force as a push or pull that changes or tends to change a body's state of rest or motion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the essential definition.

rubric.why: The SI unit of force is the newton.
rubric.description: Gives the SI unit of force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct unit.

modelAnswer: Force is a push or pull that changes or tends to change the state of rest or motion of a body.

items.followUp: Write any two advantages of friction.

rubric.why: Friction wears down surfaces in contact.
rubric.description: Gives wear and tear as a disadvantage of friction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one valid disadvantage.

rubric.why: Friction wastes energy as heat and opposes motion.
rubric.description: Gives another valid disadvantage of friction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a second, distinct disadvantage.

modelAnswer: Friction causes wear and tear of surfaces in contact.
Friction produces unwanted heat, wasting energy and reducing the efficiency of machines.

items.followUp: Write the formula for the centripetal acceleration of a body moving in a circle.

accept: keeps a body moving in a circle
rubric.why: Centripetal force acts towards the centre and keeps a body moving along a circular path.
rubric.description: Defines centripetal force and its direction or function.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct definition.

rubric.why: The centripetal force formula is mass times speed squared divided by radius.
rubric.description: Writes the formula for centripetal force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct formula.

modelAnswer: Centripetal force is the force directed towards the centre of a circular path that keeps a body moving in that path.

items.followUp: What is the resultant of two like parallel forces?

rubric.why: Like parallel forces are parallel forces acting in the same direction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that their directions are the same.

rubric.why: Unlike parallel forces are parallel forces acting in opposite directions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that their directions are opposite.

modelAnswer: Like parallel forces are parallel forces that act in the same direction.
Unlike parallel forces are parallel forces that act in opposite directions.

items.followUp: Define the moment arm of a force and state its SI unit.

rubric.why: Torque is the turning or rotational effect of a force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct meaning of torque.

rubric.why: Torque equals force multiplied by the perpendicular distance from the axis or pivot to the force's line of action.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct equation.

modelAnswer: Torque is the turning effect of a force about a pivot or axis.
Torque = force × perpendicular distance from the pivot to the line of action of the force.
